x.ASV: And in that day thou shalt say, I will give thanks unto thee, O Jehovah; for though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away and thou comfortest me.
x.Darby: And in that day thou shalt say, Jehovah, I will praise thee; for though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away, and thou hast comforted me.
x.KJV: And in that day thou shalt say, O Lord, I will praise thee: though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away, and thou comfortedst me.
x.YLT: And thou hast said in that day: `I thank thee, O Jehovah, Though Thou hast been angry with me, Turn back doth Thine anger, And Thou dost comfort me.

nt: Isaiah is using the term **day** to refer to a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when that happens]
The word **you** is singular here because Isaiah is addressing a representative Israelite. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Isaiah is using **your nose has turned back** as a common expression of the culture to mean “your anger has subsided.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your anger has subsided]

x.ASV: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid: for Jehovah, even Jehovah, is my strength and song; and he is become my salvation.
x.Darby: Behold,God is my salvation: I will trust, and not be afraid; for Jah, Jehovah, is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation.
x.KJV: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the Lord Jehovah is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation.
x.YLT: Lo, God is my salvation, I trust, and fear not, For my strength and song is Jah Jehovah, And He is to me for salvation.

nt: Isaiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Listen]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the ideas of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in other ways. Alternate translation: [God is the one saving me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [God is my Savior]

These two clauses **I will trust** and **I will not dread** mean basically the same thing. For emphasis, the author is saying it first positively and then negatively. If a speaker of your language would not use repetition like this, in your translation you can convey the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [I will confidently trust]

This line and the next one are a a quotation of [Exodus 15:2](../exo/15/02.md), which says simply “Yah.” Isaiah may be adding **Yahweh** as an explanation of the name in the quotation. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yah, that is, Yahweh]

Here Isaiah is speaking as if Yahweh were his **strength and song**. He means that Yahweh is the one who makes him strong and gives him reason to sing. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is the one who makes me strong and gives me reason to sing]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for Yah, Yahweh, makes me mighty and causes me to sing of him]

x.ASV: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.
x.Darby: And with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.
x.KJV: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.
x.YLT: And ye have drawn waters with joy Out of the fountains of salvation,

nt: Here Isaiah is speaking as if the experience of God’s salvation were **water** that could be drawn from **wells**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And joyfully you will receive salvation from God]
The word **you** is plural here because Isaiah is addressing the people of Israel as a group, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with rejoicing]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [being saved]

x.ASV: And in that day shall ye say, Give thanks unto Jehovah, call upon his name, declare his doings among the peoples, make mention that his name is exalted.
x.Darby: And in that day shall ye say, Give ye thanks to Jehovah, call upon his name, declare his deeds among the peoples, make mention that his name is exalted.
x.KJV: And in that day shall ye say, Praise the Lord, call upon his name, declare his doings among the people, make mention that his name is exalted.
x.YLT: And ye have said in that day, Give ye praise to Jehovah, call in His name. Make known among the peoples His acts. Make mention that set on high is His name.

nt: The word **you** and all of these imperatives are plural because Isaiah is addressing the people of Israel, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated the similar expression in [12:1](../12/01.md). Alternate translation: [when that happens]

Isaiah is using **call on his name** as a common expression of the culture to mean “worship him.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [worship him]

Here, Yahweh’s **name** represents his “reputation.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [his reputation is great]

The expression **his name is exalted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [he has exalted his name]

x.ASV: Sing unto Jehovah; for he hath done excellent things: let this be known in all the earth.
x.Darby: Sing psalms of Jehovah, for he hath done excellent things: this is known in all the earth.
x.KJV: Sing unto the Lord; for he hath done excellent things: this is known in all the earth.
x.YLT: Praise ye Jehovah, for excellence He hath done, Known is this in all the earth.

nt: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **majesty**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [majestic things]

The expression **this is made known** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [he has made this known]

Isaiah says **in all of the earth** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [in every land]

x.ASV: Cry aloud and shout, thou inhabitant of Zion; for great in the midst of thee is the Holy One of Israel.
x.Darby: Cry out and shout, thou inhabitress of Zion; for great is the Holy One of Israel in the midst of thee.
x.KJV: Cry out and shout, thou inhabitant of Zion: for great is the Holy One of Israel in the midst of thee.
x.YLT: Cry aloud, and sing, O inhabitant of Zion, For great in thy midst is the Holy One of Israel!'

nt: The imperatives **Cry aloud** and **should joyfully** and the participle **dweller** are feminine singular. Isaiah is addressing a representative female resident of **Zion**. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction, and use the feminine form f your language marks that distinction.

The terms **Cry aloud** and **shout joyfully** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Shout for joy]

In this verse, the word **dweller** is singular in form, but it refers to all the inhabitants of Zion as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “dweller.” Alternate translation: [inhabitants of Zion]

Isaiah is using the adjective **Holy** as a noun to refer to God. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the holy God of Israel]
